item.title: A Curvilinear-Grid Eikonal Framework for Passive Seismic Source Location in Anisotropic Media: Theory and Numerical Validation
item.description: The accurate localization of passive seismic sources is important for geophysical applications, such as reservoir characterization and seismic-hazard assessment. Traveltime-based location methods are widely used for this purpose, but their accuracy can be significantly affected by complex surface topography and seismic anisotropy, which alter seismic traveltimes and may lead to biased source parameters when these effects are neglected or inadequately represented. To address this issue, we develop a passive-source location framework based on a topography-dependent eikonal equation (TDEE) formulated for anisotropic media on boundary-conforming curvilinear grids. The hypocenter is determined by globally minimizing a station-pair double-difference (DD) traveltime objective function, in which the origin time is eliminated, and the origin time is subsequently estimated from the absolute-traveltime residuals with the hypocenter fixed. Synthetic experiments involving complex topography and anisotropy are conducted to evaluate the accuracy, computational performance, and sensitivity of the method to observational and modeling errors. The results show that the proposed framework provides accurate hypocenter and origin-time estimates under various model configurations, whereas neglecting topographic or anisotropic effects can produce systematic biases in the estimated source parameters. The proposed method provides an effective traveltime-based approach for passive-source location in complex topographic and anisotropic media.

item.title: DGAFNet: A Dual-Branch Gradually Cross-Attention Fusion Network for Precipitation Nowcasting
item.description: Short-term precipitation forecasting is critical for transportation, agriculture, and disaster management, where accurate and timely predictions can significantly reduce risks and improve decision-making. However, traditional methods such as numerical weather prediction (NWP) and radar echo extrapolation often fail to capture fine-grained spatiotemporal dynamics, especially under high-intensity precipitation. To alleviate this issue, we propose a dual-branch gradually cross-attention fusion network (DGAFNet) based on locality-aware SwinLSTM (LASL), which fully captures the spatiotemporal evolution of precipitation by integrating multisource data from radar and satellite observations. In DGAFNet, the satellite branch is tailored to model global–local spatial dependencies, while the radar branch is specifically designed to exploit multiscale features by utilizing atrous spatial pyramid pooling (ASPP). In addition, we introduce a gradually cross-attention fusion module (GCAFM), which leverages attention mechanisms to adaptively highlight key informative regions and dynamically merges features from the dual branches at multiple levels. Experimental results on the storm event imagery (SEVIR) dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art models (ConvLSTM, PredRNN++, SwinLSTM-B and CM-STJointNet) across metrics, especially under high-intensity precipitation scenarios. These results highlight DGAFNets ability to effectively combine multisource data for more accurate and timely precipitation forecasting.

item.title: Surrogate-Assisted Physics-Guided Retrieval of Range-Varying Evaporation Duct Height From Radar Sea Clutter
item.description: Retrieving a range-varying evaporation duct height (EDH) trajectory from radar sea clutter is ill-posed, while repeatedly coupling a high-fidelity propagation solver to inversion is computationally prohibitive. This article presents Physics-ResCNN, a surrogate-assisted framework that transfers parabolic-equation (PE) knowledge to inverse-model training without adding environmental covariates or forward calculations at deployment. A residual-convolutional surrogate first learns the mapping from range-dependent duct states to PE propagation loss. Once frozen, it combines with a sea-clutter observation model to penalize disagreement between the observed clutter and that reconstructed from the retrieved duct profile. The resulting inverse network maps a 500-point centered clutter profile directly to a 101-node EDH trajectory and duct-presence mask. On a leakage-controlled, day-grouped East China Sea synthetic benchmark for 2025 under a fixed radar configuration with 3571 test profiles, Physics-ResCNN achieves 0.659-m RMSE and 0.290-m MAE, reducing RMSE by 18.6% relative to an identical supervised ResCNN. Ablation and direct-PE analyses support the observation-consistency mechanism. Buffered spatial holdouts yield smaller, seed-dependent gains than the nominal benchmark, and within-family refractivity-gradient perturbations retain lower aggregate RMSE with some tail-error reversals. The framework, therefore, provides an efficient means of embedding offline propagation physics into clutter-only, range-resolved refractivity from clutter (RFC) inference.
item.authors: Yi Yan;Jiangting Li;Lixin Guo;Yuxuan Wang;Shuji Sun;Tong Xu;Zonghua Ding;

item.title: DPEE-STGAN: A Dual-Path Encoding-Embedded Style Transfer GAN for Multidomain Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation
item.description: The spectral and radiometric characteristics of remote sensing imagery can vary substantially across sensors, geographic regions, and acquisition conditions, resulting in pronounced domain shifts. Consequently, semantic segmentation models trained on a source domain often suffer severe performance degradation when directly applied to heterogeneous target-domain imagery. To address this issue, we propose an unsupervised domain-adaptive segmentation framework based on image style transfer and introduce DPEE-STGAN, a dual-path encoding-embedded style transfer generative adversarial network (GAN). DPEE-STGAN separates style conditioning into an intrinsic path that preserves source-domain geometry and texture, and an extrinsic path that injects target-domain appearance cues through hierarchical structure and color control. The resulting pseudotarget images retain the source annotations and are used to fine-tune a source-pretrained segmentation model without target-domain labels. Experiments on heterogeneous uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) and satellite datasets demonstrate consistent improvements in both style transfer and cross-domain segmentation. DPEE-STGAN achieves the lowest source-referenced learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS) among the compared methods in all six evaluated transfer settings. For Potsdam $\rightarrow $ Vaihingen and Vaihingen $\rightarrow $ Potsdam, the proposed framework reaches 72.85%/48.12% and 68.43%/40.27% in overall accuracy (OA)/mIoU, respectively, improving mIoU over the corresponding source-only baselines by 12.10 and 10.41 percentage points. Across 11 additional heterogeneous target domains, the mean building intersection over union (IoU) increases from 35.20% to 50.14%. These results show that explicitly decoupling source-content preservation from target-style injection provides an effective solution for semantic segmentation under substantial remote sensing domain shifts.

item.title: Design and Validation of an Integrated Long-Wave Infrared and Laser Detection Optical System for Space Remote Sensing
item.description: Space target detection faces key challenges, including weak-signal extraction, complex background interference, and target range acquisition. To address these challenges, this article proposes a novel space target detection approach based on the synergy of infrared imaging and laser ranging. By developing an integrated dual-channel detection optical system comprising a long-wave infrared (LWIR) channel and a laser receiving channel, multisource information fusion and complementary functionality are achieved. Optical simulation results show that the LWIR channel has an F-number ( $F^{\#}$ ) of 2, and the full-field modulation transfer function (MTF) at the Nyquist frequency of 20 lp/mm exceeds 0.2 at the simulated temperatures of $0~^{\circ }$ C, $20~^{\circ }$ C, $30~^{\circ }$ C, and $40~^{\circ }$ C, approaching the diffraction limit and demonstrating good imaging performance. By optimizing the YNI and I/IBAR parameters in conjunction with LightTools stray-light analysis, the Narcissus-induced image-plane nonuniformity is effectively suppressed, resulting in a uniform focal-plane energy distribution. The laser receiving channel exhibits good energy concentration, with more than 90% encircled energy within a $40~\mu $ m diameter, and provides precise ranging capability. After integration, the dual-channel opto-mechanical system achieves a compact and miniaturized common-aperture configuration. An engineering prototype was fabricated and experimentally evaluated through wavefront testing, resolution testing, outdoor imaging, simulated space-target imaging, and laser ranging accuracy tests. The measured wavefront error after optical alignment is root-mean-square (rms) $0.067\lambda $ , and the rms static ranging error is 0.724 m (approximately 0.72 m). Ground-based imaging experiments show that the measured focal-plane grayscale distribution is consistent with the uniform energy-distribution trend predicted by the LightTools simulations, providing experimental support for the effectiveness of the Narcissus suppression design. The LWIR and laser channels provide complementary target imaging and range information, respectively, demonstrating the feasibility of the proposed dual-channel integrated optical system. This work provides a practical common-aperture optical design solution for compact and highly integrated space remote sensing and space situational awareness (SSA) payloads.
item.authors: Lei Zhang;Bo Li;Jize Fan;Xu Zhang;Zihui Zhang;Xiaoxu Wang;Pingping Chen;Zhennan Li;

item.title: Physics-Informed BiLSTM Network for Atmospheric Temperature and Humidity Profiles Retrieval From Ground-Based Infrared Hyperspectral Interferometers
item.description: Atmospheric temperature and humidity profiles are essential for numerical weather prediction (NWP) and climate research. Ground-based hyperspectral infrared spectrometers provide rich radiance information, yet traditional physical retrievals are computationally expensive, while statistical approaches struggle with complex nonlinear radiance–state relationships. Purely data-driven deep learning methods improve efficiency but often lack physical consistency, limiting their reliability under unseen atmospheric conditions. To address these limitations, this study proposes a physics-informed bidirectional long short-term memory (Phy-BiLSTM) framework to retrieve boundary-layer temperature and humidity profiles from Atmospheric Emitted Radiance Interferometer (AERI) hyperspectral radiance. The model incorporates two complementary forms of physical knowledge: 1) a BiLSTM architecture that captures vertical coupling and interlevel dependencies within the atmospheric column, physically motivated by the fact that atmospheric states are influenced by both lower and upper levels; and 2) thermodynamic consistency constraints, derived from radiative–thermodynamic balance and potential temperature continuity, which are directly embedded into the loss function during training to actively enforce physically plausible solutions. Trained on AERI and radiosonde observations from 2006 to 2016 and evaluated on an independent 2017 dataset at the Southern Great Plains (SGP) site, Phy-BiLSTM achieves root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) of 0.85 K for temperature and 1.00 g/kg for humidity, outperforming benchmark deep learning methods in capturing vertical atmospheric gradients within the 0–3 km boundary layer. Compared to the standard physical retrieval method AERIoe, Phy-BiLSTM reduces temperature and humidity RMSE by 24.1% and 23.7%, respectively, while accelerating inference from approximately 8.96 min per profile to 3.985 ms per sample on graphics processing unit (GPU)—a speedup of over 135 $000\times $ . Furthermore, long-term evaluations demonstrate the model’s robustness in reproducing the climatological annual cycle and capturing extreme events, such as the 2011 and 2012 summer heatwaves. Ablation experiments confirm that both the BiLSTM structure and thermodynamic constraints are critical to the model’s performance.
item.authors: Yangyang Song;Wanxia Deng;Lei Liu;Jinfeng Ding;Wei Huang;

item.title: Fast and Accurate Inversion Method of Asteroid Physical Parameters With a Lycaon Pictus Hunting Algorithm
item.description: The inversion of physical parameters of asteroids is a core technology for planetary exploration engineering. There are two key limitations to traditional approaches: the objective function is nearly flat in certain parameter subspaces, making the corresponding chi-square values almost identical, while exhaustive sampling over the entire parameter space incurs prohibitive computational costs. To address these issues, we propose weakly observable subspace theory, which proves the existence of a weakly observable subspace in the parameter space where the objective function is approximately flat, making it difficult to distinguish physical parameter vectors of asteroids with high errors. Under the guidance of this theory, we propose a fast and accurate inversion method with a Lycaon pictus hunting algorithm (LPHA). This approach is inspired by two unique hunting mechanisms of Lycaon pictus, including region lock and roaming hunt. In region lock, we use singular value decomposition (SVD) of high-order derivative information and the Hessian matrix to estimate the weakly observable subspace, which is locked as the hunting region. In roaming hunt, we perform concentrated sampling in that subspace followed by Levenberg–Marquardt (LM) refinement. This framework provides mathematical characterization of the weakly observable subspace and translates biological hunting into a sampling scheme, reducing unnecessary Monte Carlo (MC) samples. Simulation results on multiple asteroids demonstrate that LPHA achieves over 60% reduction in estimation errors while requiring only 10.13% of the computation time of the conventional LM approach. LPHA provides a fast, accurate, and theoretically grounded solution for asteroid physical parameter inversion, with broad applicability to other high-dimensional nonlinear inverse problems.
item.authors: Yangyang Li;Jin Liu;Zhiwei Kang;Xiaolin Ning;Xin Ma;Jiancheng Fang;

item.title: SGHFNet: A Saliency-Guided High-Frequency Enhancement Network for Infrared Small Target Detection
item.description: Transformer-based methods have achieved promising results in infrared small target detection (IRSTD) by capturing global context and long-range spatial dependencies. However, unconstrained global interactions may weaken the responses of dim, low-contrast targets. Moreover, modeling only in the spatial domain makes it difficult to distinguish true targets from target-like noise and structured background clutter. These limitations can lead to false alarms and missed detections in complex infrared scenes. To address these challenges, we propose a saliency-guided high-frequency enhancement network (SGHFNet), which inserts a saliency-guided global fusion (SGGF) block into the encoder–decoder skip connections. The SGGF block comprises two components: 1) saliency-guided cross-attention (SGCA) introduces a saliency-guided bias to regulate cross-level channel interactions and preserve weak target responses and 2) spectral-gated feed-forward network (SGFFN) combines multiscale depthwise convolution with adaptive high-pass filtering (AHPF) to enhance target boundaries and local structures. Experiments on NUAA-SIRST, NUDT-SIRST, and IRSTD-1K show that SGHFNet achieves competitive performance compared with 19 representative methods. Ablation studies further show that SGCA and SGFFN provide complementary gains in target recovery and false-alarm control.

item.title: SSUC-CD: A Self-Supervised and Unsupervised Collaborative Framework for Automatic Change Detection in Multitemporal Remote Sensing Images
item.description: Automatic change detection offers the significant advantage of eliminating reliance on costly and labor-intensive manual annotation data, and has become a research hotspot in the field of remote sensing information extraction. However, existing studies typically employ self-supervised learning or unsupervised learning independently and lack self-supervised learning strategies specifically designed for change detection. To address this limitation, we propose a self-supervised and unsupervised collaborative change detection (SSUC-CD) framework, which is applicable to both homogeneous and heterogeneous remote sensing images. During each training epoch, the model first performs self-supervised learning on simulated change data, followed by unsupervised learning on real multitemporal images. First, SSUC-CD utilizes the class information in remote sensing images as the source of self-supervised signals tailored for change detection. By dynamically generating simulated change data based on the real-world multitemporal images, the model gradually learns the true ability to represent and extract change information by self-supervised learning. Second, SSUC-CD leverages unsupervised change detection learning on real-world multitemporal images to further refine the model’s change detection capability. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, experiments were conducted across six datasets. Compared with 20 state-of-the-art methods, the proposed method significantly improves the automation level and reliability of change detection without requiring manually labeled sample data. The complete source code of this method will be made publicly available at the following website upon publication: https://github.com/huifuzhuang/SSUC-CD
item.authors: Huifu Zhuang;Yuli Zhang;Xiang Zhang;Yu Zhang;Zhong Lu;Ming Hao;Hua Zhang;José Fernández;Sen Du;

item.title: SFDA-Net: Spatial–Frequency Dual-Branch Autoencoder Network for Hyperspectral Unmixing
item.description: Hyperspectral unmixing (HU) aims to estimate endmember spectra and fractional abundances from mixed pixels and is a fundamental task in remote sensing image analysis. Despite recent advances in deep learning-based blind unmixing, three challenges remain. First, many convolutional unmixing networks rely primarily on local operations, which limits their ability to capture long-range spatial–spectral dependencies and broad spatial distribution patterns. Second, the global pooling used in some attention mechanisms may weaken pixel-level coordinate information, which is important for dense abundance estimation and the preservation of spatial structures. Third, topographic effects and nonuniform illumination cause spectral magnitude variations, which may bias abundance estimation when a single linear decoder is shared across pixels. To address these issues, we propose SFDA-Net, a spatial–frequency dual-branch autoencoder (AE) for HU. First, a dual-branch feature extraction module (DFEM) combines learnable frequency-dependent Fourier filtering with local spatial convolution. The frequency branch captures long-range spatial dependencies, whereas the spatial branch preserves local neighborhood structure. Second, a coordinate attention module (CAM) uses separate horizontal and vertical encodings to recalibrate features, thereby retaining coordinate information during feature aggregation. Third, an intensity decoupling strategy (IDS) uses scale-normalized spectra for encoder-side representation learning and restores the observed spectral norm before reconstruction in the original reflectance domain. Experiments on two simulated datasets and four real or physically rendered datasets indicate that SFDA-Net provides reliable endmember extraction and abundance estimation across the evaluated datasets.
item.authors: Chen Ding;Rundong Liu;Yizhuo Dong;Pengfei Wan;Canyu Zhang;Wenqiang Hua;Song Yan;Lei Zhang;Wei Wei;

item.title: Enhanced Denoising and Terrain Sample Densification of ICESat-2 Data Using a Bayesian Signal Model
item.description: The reliability of Ice, Cloud, and Land Elevation Satellite (ICESat-2) terrain height retrieval depends heavily on effective photon denoising. However, uneven background noise often complicates conventional feature-based methods, leading to the erroneous rejection of crucial signal photons. To address this, this article introduces a Bayesian signal model (BSM) as a postprocessing framework designed to recover these misidentified photons and enhance ICESat-2/ATL08 photon-denoising accuracy, thereby increasing the number of reliable terrain height samples. The BSM innovatively leverages initial ATL08 outcomes to structure a K-nearest neighbor (KNN)-derived likelihood function, generating a robust heuristic normalized score for the retrieval of missed signal photons. Subsequently, this metric is applied within a sliding-window-based detection and refinement procedure, where the definitive identification of these missed signal photons is achieved via local Otsu thresholding constrained by ICESat-2 quality parameters to minimize the inclusion of true noise. Experimental results over large-scale regions demonstrate that, within the processing windows where the BSM performs signal recovery, the approach achieves an average overall Accuracy (OA) of 0.94, compared with 0.84 for the standard ATL08. Furthermore, after the adopted quality-control screening, the method substantially increases the density of valid terrain samples while maintaining vertical accuracy comparable to that of ATL08, validating the effectiveness of the BSM for large-scale geodetic control and digital elevation modeling. The reported denoising and terrain-retrieval metrics are therefore conditional on the adopted data-selection and quality-control procedures and should not be interpreted as global performance over the full range of ICESat-2 observations and conditions.
item.authors: Zilong He;Zhiwei Li;Mi Jiang;Yushan Zhou;Chuwei Zhang;Xin He;Minzheng Mu;Chang Gu;Fukang Qiao;Yongze Song;

item.title: Agent-Inspired Recurrent Control of Spectral-Composition Logits With Latent Condition Prototype Routing for Pansharpening
item.description: Pansharpening aims to reconstruct a high-resolution multispectral (HRMS) image from a low-resolution multispectral (MS) image and a high-resolution panchromatic (PAN) image. Although deep-learning-based methods have improved spatial–spectral representation, most still introduce PAN details through pixel-, residual-, or feature-level fusion, offering limited control over how spatial structures are assigned to spectral components. Many progressive methods also rely on repeated refinement blocks with limited adaptation to the current reconstruction state and refinement history. These limitations may cause detail misallocation, spectral distortion, or error accumulation under spatially varying PAN–MS observation mismatch. To address these limitations, we propose spectral-composition recurrent control for pansharpening (SCoRe-Pan), an agent-inspired recurrent control framework that recurrently updates spectral-composition logits, which describe pixel associations with learnable spectral components before normalization, and reconstructs the HRMS image through adaptive spectral-basis mixing. The recurrent controller follows a fully differentiable observation–history–condition–control procedure, integrating observation-state encoding, history memory (HM) retrieval, and stagewise control prediction, while condition prototype routing (CPR) adapts the update strategy to different PAN–MS observation states (OSs). Experiments on WorldView-II, QuickBird, and Maryland under reduced-resolution, full-resolution, cross-dataset generalization, robustness, ablation, and efficiency settings show that SCoRe-Pan achieves competitive or superior spatial–spectral reconstruction quality compared with representative traditional and deep-learning-based pansharpening methods. Our code can be found at https://github.com/Rui0913/SCoRe-Pan.
item.authors: Rui Hao;Xin Jin;Puming Wang;Hongyue Huang;Cheng Xie;Qian Jiang;
